questions.q: In a circuit containing a pure resistor connected to an AC source,
options: Voltage and current are in same phase with each other
questions.explanation: For a pure resistor, current and voltage reach their peak and zero values simultaneously, i.e., they are in phase.

questions.q: A light bulb rated 100 W is connected to an AC source of 220 V, 50 Hz. The rms current through the bulb is

A small town with a demand of 900 kW of electric power at 220 V is situated 20 km away from an electric power generating station. The two-wires line has resistance per unit length of $5\times10^{-4}\ \Omega m^{-1}$. The town gets power from the line through 45000 V to 220 V stepdown transformer at a substation in the town. The line power loss in the form of heat is
questions.explanation: Power is transmitted at 45000V, so line current I = P/V = 900000/45000 = 20A. Total line resistance = $5\times10^{-4}\times(2\times20000)=20\,\Omega$. Power loss = I²R = 400×20 = 8000W = 8 kW.

questions.q: In domestic electric mains supply, the voltage and the current are
questions.explanation: Domestic mains supply an alternating voltage which drives an alternating current through the load.

questions.q: A sinusoidal voltage produced by an AC generator at any instant t is given by an equation V = 311 sin 314 t. The rms value of voltage and frequency are respectively
questions.explanation: $V_{rms}=311/\sqrt2\approx220$ V, and $\omega=314=2\pi f$ gives $f=50$ Hz.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit containing an AC source of 100 V has an inductor and a capacitor of reactances 24 Ω and 16 Ω respectively. If a resistance of 6 Ω is connected in series, then the potential difference across the series combination of inductor and capacitor only is
questions.explanation: $Z=\sqrt{6^2+(24-16)^2}=10\,\Omega$, so $I=100/10=10$ A. Voltage across (L–C) combination $=I(X_L-X_C)=10\times8=80$ V.

questions.q: In an LCR series circuit, the value of only capacitance C is varied. The resulting variation of resonance frequency $f_0$ as a function of C can be represented as [four candidate f0-vs-C graphs: (A) rises then falls, (B) straight line rising, (C) decreasing convex curve, (D) decreasing then rising]
options: a curve that rises and then falls
a straight line increasing with C
a decreasing convex curve approaching the C-axis
a curve that falls and then rises
questions.explanation: $f_0=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt C}$, which is a monotonically decreasing curve as C increases.

questions.q: The figure shows variation of R, $X_L$ and $X_C$ with frequency 'f' in a series LCR circuit [XC falls with frequency, XL rises with frequency, R is a constant horizontal line; points A, B, C, D are marked on the frequency axis in increasing order, with the XL-XC crossing near C/D]. Then for what frequency point is the circuit capacitive?
questions.explanation: The circuit is capacitive when $X_C>X_L$, i.e. at frequencies below the resonance (crossing) point; among the marked points this is point A.

questions.q: In series LCR circuit at resonance, the phase difference between voltage and current is
questions.explanation: At resonance the impedance of a series LCR circuit is purely resistive, so voltage and current are in phase (phase difference zero).

questions.q: An ideal transformer has a turns ratio of 10. When the primary is connected to 220 V, 50 Hz ac source, the power output is
questions.explanation: An ideal transformer has no power loss, so the output power always equals the input power regardless of the turns ratio.

questions.q: Total impedance of a series LCR circuit varies with angular frequency of the AC source connected to it as shown in the graph [Z vs ω curve, minimum Z$_{min}$ near ω=500 rad/s, with Z=√2 Z$_{min}$ at ω=400 and ω=600 rad/s]. The quality factor Q of the series LCR circuit is
questions.explanation: The bandwidth is $\Delta\omega$ = 600−400 = 200 rad/s at resonance $\omega_0$=500 rad/s, so Q = $\omega_0/\Delta\omega$ = 500/200 = 2.5.

questions.q: An alternating current is given by $i=i_1\sin\omega t+i_2\cos\omega t$. The r.m.s. current is given by
questions.explanation: For two out-of-phase sinusoidal components of the same frequency, the rms value combines as $\sqrt{\dfrac{i_1^2+i_2^2}{2}}$.

questions.q: A fully charged capacitor 'C' with initial charge 'q$_0$' is connected to a coil of self inductance 'L' at t = 0. The time at which the energy is stored equally between the electric and the magnetic field is
questions.explanation: The charge oscillates as $q=q_0\cos\omega t$ with $\omega=1/\sqrt{LC}$. The energies are equal when $q=q_0/\sqrt2$, i.e. when $\omega t=\pi/4$, giving $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}\sqrt{LC}$.

questions.q: A series resonant ac circuit contains a capacitance 10$^{-6}$ F and an inductor of 10$^{-4}$ H. The frequency of electrical oscillations will be
questions.explanation: $f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{10^{-4}\times10^{-6}}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\times10^{-5}}=\dfrac{10^5}{2\pi}$ Hz.

questions.q: In a series LCR circuit R = 300 $\Omega$, L = 0.9 H, C = 2.0 $\mu$F and $\omega$ = 1000 rad/sec., then impedance of the circuit is
questions.explanation: $X_L=\omega L=1000\times0.9=900\ \Omega$; $X_C=\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=\dfrac{1}{1000\times2\times10^{-6}}=500\ \Omega$. $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}=\sqrt{300^2+400^2}=500\ \Omega$.

questions.q: What will be the reading in the voltmeter and ammeter of the circuit shown? (Circuit: a resistor R=45Ω in series with a 90V AC source and an ammeter A forms the outer loop; this feeds a branch containing a capacitor X$_C$=4Ω in series with an inductor X$_L$=4Ω, with a voltmeter V connected in parallel with this L-C branch.)
questions.explanation: Since X$_L$=X$_C$, the series L-C branch is at resonance and has zero net impedance, i.e. it behaves as a short circuit; the voltmeter, connected across this short, reads 0 V. The full source voltage then drops across R alone, so the ammeter reads I = 90V/45$\Omega$ = 2 A.

questions.q: LC oscillations are similar and analogous to the mechanical oscillations of a block attached to a spring. The electrical equivalent of the force constant of the spring is
questions.explanation: Comparing energies $\tfrac12 L\dot q^2 \leftrightarrow \tfrac12 mv^2$ and $\tfrac{q^2}{2C}\leftrightarrow\tfrac12 kx^2$ shows $L\leftrightarrow m$ and $\dfrac{1}{C}\leftrightarrow k$, so the spring constant corresponds to the reciprocal of capacitance.

questions.q: In an oscillating LC circuit, L = 3.00 mH and C = 2.70 μF. At t = 0 the charge on the capacitor is zero and the current is 2.00A. The maximum charge that will appear on the capacitor will be:
questions.explanation: Energy conservation: $\tfrac12 LI^2=\tfrac{Q_{max}^2}{2C}\Rightarrow Q_{max}=I\sqrt{LC}=2\sqrt{(3\times10^{-3})(2.7\times10^{-6})}=18\times10^{-5}$ C.

questions.q: In the given circuit the peak voltages across C, L and R are 30 V, 110 V and 60 V respectively. The rms value of the applied voltage is
questions.explanation: Peak applied voltage $=\sqrt{(V_L-V_C)^2+V_R^2}=\sqrt{80^2+60^2}=100$ V, so rms value $=100/\sqrt2=70.7$ V.

questions.q: The power factor of a R-L circuit is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$. If the inductive reactance is 2 $\Omega$, the value of resistance is
questions.explanation: $\cos\phi=R/Z=1/\sqrt3 \Rightarrow Z=\sqrt3 R \Rightarrow R^2+X_L^2=3R^2 \Rightarrow R=X_L/\sqrt2=\sqrt2\,\Omega$.

questions.q: In the given circuit, the resonant frequency is [inductor 0.5 mH in parallel with capacitor 20 $\mu$F]
questions.explanation: $f=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{0.5\times10^{-3}\times20\times10^{-6}}}\approx1592$ Hz.

questions.q: The frequency of an alternating current is 50 Hz. What is the minimum time taken by current to reach its peak value from rms value ?
questions.explanation: Current is at rms value when $\sin\omega t = 1/\sqrt2$, i.e. $\omega t = \pi/4$, giving $t = T/8 = (1/50)/8 = 2.5\times10^{-3}$ s to reach the peak.

questions.q: [Circuit shows an inductor L, capacitor C and resistor R = 100 $\Omega$ in series across a 220 V, 50 Hz AC source, with an ammeter A in the main line and a voltmeter V across R; the voltmeter across L reads V$_L$ = 50 V and across C reads V$_C$ = 50 V] The readings of ammeter and voltmeter in the following circuit are respectively
questions.explanation: Since V$_L$ = V$_C$, they cancel at resonance and the entire supply voltage appears across R: I = 220/100 = 2.2 A, and the voltmeter across R reads the full 220 V.

questions.q: An inductor of inductance L and resistor R are joined together in series and connected by a source of frequency $\omega$. The power dissipated in the circuit is
questions.explanation: Impedance $Z=\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2L^2}$, rms current $I=V/Z$, and power $P=I^2R = V^2R/(R^2+\omega^2L^2)$.

questions.q: Which of the following, represents the variation of inductive reactance (X$_L$) with the frequency of voltage source ($\nu$)?
options: A straight line through the origin rising with $\nu$
A curve starting flat near the origin and curving increasingly steeply upward as $\nu$ increases
A curve rising steeply from near the origin and then flattening as $\nu$ increases
A curve falling from a high value with $\nu$
questions.explanation: X$_L$ = 2$\pi\nu$L is directly proportional to frequency, so it is represented by a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: A 100 W bulb is connected to an AC source of 220 V, 50 Hz. Then the current flowing through the bulb is
In the series LCR circuit, the power dissipation is through
questions.explanation: In an ideal series LCR circuit, only the resistor R dissipates power; the ideal inductor and capacitor do not dissipate energy on average.

questions.q: In Karnataka, the normal domestic power supply AC is 220 V, 50 Hz. Here 220 V and 50 Hz refer to
options: Peak value of voltage and frequency
rms value of voltage and frequency
Mean value of voltage and frequency
Peak value of voltage and angular frequency
questions.explanation: The voltage and frequency ratings quoted for AC mains are conventionally the rms value of voltage and the frequency.

questions.q: A step-up transformer operates on a 230 V line and a load current of 2 A. The ratio of primary and secondary windings is 1 : 25. Then the current in the primary is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, I$_p$N$_p$ = I$_s$N$_s$ ⟹ I$_p$ = I$_s$(N$_s$/N$_p$) = 2 × 25 = 50 A.

questions.q: The output of a step down transformer is measured to be 48 V when connected to a 12 W bulb. The value of peak current is
questions.explanation: $I_{rms} = \dfrac{P}{V} = \dfrac{12}{48} = 0.25$ A. Peak current $=\sqrt2\,I_{rms} = 0.25\sqrt2 = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt2}$ A.

questions.q: A coil of inductive reactance $1/\sqrt3\,\Omega$ and resistance 1 Ω is connected to a 200 V, 50 Hz A.C. supply. The time lag between maximum voltage and current is
questions.explanation: $\tan\phi = X_L/R = 1/\sqrt3 \Rightarrow \phi = 30° = \pi/6$ rad. Time lag $= \phi/\omega = \dfrac{\pi/6}{2\pi\times50} = \dfrac{1}{600}$ s.

questions.q: The rms value of current in a 50 Hz AC circuit is 6 A. The average value of AC current over a cycle is
questions.explanation: The average of a sinusoidal current over one complete cycle is always zero.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 10 $\mu$F is connected to an AC source and an AC Ammeter. If the source voltage varies as V = $50\sqrt2\sin100t$, the reading of the ammeter is
questions.explanation: $X_C=\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=\dfrac{1}{100\times10\times10^{-6}}=1000\,\Omega$. $I_{rms}=\dfrac{V_{rms}}{X_C}=\dfrac{50}{1000}=50$ mA.

questions.q: In a series L.C.R circuit, the potential drop across L, C and R respectively are 40 V, 120 V and 60 V. Then the source voltage is

In a series L.C.R. circuit an alternating emf (v) and current (i) are given by the equation $v=v_0\sin\omega t$, $i=i_0\sin\left(\omega t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$. The average power dissipated in the circuit over a cycle of AC is
questions.explanation: $P_{avg}=\dfrac{1}{2}v_0i_0\cos\phi=\dfrac{1}{2}v_0i_0\cos60°=\dfrac{v_0i_0}{4}$.

questions.q: In an LCR circuit, at resonance
options: the current and voltage are in phase
the current leads the voltage by $\pi/2$
questions.explanation: At resonance, $X_L=X_C$, so the impedance is purely resistive and the current is in phase with the voltage.

questions.q: A transformer is used to light a 100 W – 110 V lamp from 220 V mains. If the main current is 0.5 A, the efficiency of the transformer is
questions.explanation: Input power = 220×0.5 = 110 W; output (lamp) power = 100 W; efficiency = 100/110 ≈ 90%.

questions.q: The average power dissipated in a pure inductor is
questions.explanation: In a pure inductor, current lags voltage by 90°, so the average power (∝ cos90° = 0) dissipated is zero.

questions.q: A multimeter reads a voltage of a certain A.C. source as 100 V. What is the peak value of voltage of A.C. source?
questions.explanation: Multimeters read rms values; V$_0$ = V$_{rms}$\times\sqrt{2} = 100\times1.414 = 141.4 V.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit contains inductance 5 mH, capacitance 2 $\mu$F and resistance 10 $\Omega$. If a frequency A.C. source is varied, what is the frequency at which maximum power is dissipated?
questions.explanation: Maximum power occurs at resonance: f = 1/(2$\pi\sqrt{LC}$) = 1/(2$\pi\sqrt{5\times10^{-3}\times2\times10^{-6}}$) = 1/(2$\pi\times10^{-4}$) = (5/$\pi$)\times10^3 Hz.

questions.q: A step down transformer has 50 turns on secondary and 1000 turns on primary winding. If a transformer is connected to 220 V 1A A.C. source, what is output current of the transformer?
The average power dissipated in A.C. circuit is 2 watt. If a current flowing through a circuit is 2 A and impedance is 1 $\Omega$, what is the power factor of the AC circuit?
questions.explanation: P = I^2 Z \cos\phi \Rightarrow 2 = (2)^2(1)\cos\phi \Rightarrow \cos\phi = 0.5.

questions.q: For a transformer, the turns ratio is 3 and its efficiency is 0.75. The current flowing in the primary coil is 2 A and the voltage applied to it is 100 V. Then the voltage and the current flowing in the secondary coil are ________ respectively.
questions.explanation: Step-up turns ratio 3 gives $V_s=3\times100=300$ V. Input power $=100\times2=200$ W; output power $=0.75\times200=150$ W; $I_s=150/300=0.5$ A.

questions.q: In R-L-C series circuit, the potential differences across each element is 20 V. Now the value of the resistance alone is doubled, then P.D. across R, L and C respectively
questions.explanation: Equal PDs across R, L, C mean the circuit is at resonance ($X_L=X_C=R$ numerically) with source voltage 20 V. Doubling $R$ preserves resonance ($X_L=X_C$ unchanged), halving the current; $V_R$ stays 20 V (since $Z=R$ at resonance, so $V_R=$ source voltage), while $V_L=V_C$ each halve to 10 V.

questions.q: A series combination of resistor (R), capacitor (C) is connected to an A.C. source of angular frequency '$\omega$'. Keeping the voltage same, if the frequency is changed to $\omega$/3, the current becomes half of the original current. Then the ratio of the capacitive reactance and resistance at the former frequency is
questions.explanation: Same voltage, halved current, and $X_C$ tripling (since $\omega\to\omega/3$) at the same $R$ gives $Z_2=2Z_1$: $R^2+9X_C^2=4(R^2+X_C^2)\Rightarrow5X_C^2=3R^2\Rightarrow X_C/R=\sqrt{0.6}$.

questions.q: A resistor of 500 $\Omega$, an inductance of 0.5 H are in series with an a.c. which is given by V = 100$\sqrt2$ sin(1000 t). The power factor of the combination is
questions.explanation: $X_L=\omega L=1000\times0.5=500\ \Omega$; power factor $=R/Z=500/\sqrt{500^2+500^2}=1/\sqrt2$.

questions.q: An ideal resistance R, ideal inductance L, ideal capacitance C and AC volt meters V$_1$, V$_2$, V$_3$ and V$_4$ are connected to an AC source as shown [figure: R, L, C in parallel branches with V$_1$ across R, V$_2$ across L, V$_3$ across C, V$_4$ across the source]. At resonance,
options: reading in V$_3$ = reading in V$_1$
reading in V$_1$ = reading in V$_2$
reading in V$_2$ = reading in V$_4$
reading in V$_2$ = reading in V$_3$
questions.explanation: At resonance $X_L=X_C$, so the voltage across the inductor equals the voltage across the capacitor in magnitude: V$_2$ = V$_3$.

questions.q: In an A.C. circuit, $V$ and $I$ are given by $V = 150\,Sin(150t)$ volt and $I = 150\,Sin\left(150t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ ampere. The power dissipated in the circuit is .................
questions.explanation: Average power $=V_{rms}I_{rms}\cos\phi=\dfrac{150}{\sqrt2}\times\dfrac{150}{\sqrt2}\times\cos60^0=\dfrac{150^2}{2}\times0.5=5625$ W.

questions.q: In the series L-C-R circuit shown, the impedance is ............ [Circuit: an inductor $L=1H$, a capacitor $C=20\mu F$ and a resistor $R=300\,\Omega$ in series, connected to an AC source of 50 V and frequency $\dfrac{50}{\pi}$ Hz]
questions.explanation: $\omega=2\pi f=100$ rad/s; $X_L=\omega L=100\,\Omega$, $X_C=1/(\omega C)=500\,\Omega$; $Z=\sqrt{R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2}=\sqrt{300^2+400^2}=500\,\Omega$.

questions.q: A transformer works on the principle of .................
options: magnetic effect of the electrical current
questions.explanation: A transformer transfers energy between coils through mutual induction.

questions.q: In a series resonant R–L–C circuit, the voltage across $R$ is 100 V and the value of $R=1000\,\Omega$. The capacitance of the capacitor is $2\times10^{-6}$ F; angular frequency of AC is 200 rad s$^{-1}$. Then the P.D. across the inductance coil is .....................
questions.explanation: $I=V_R/R=100/1000=0.1$ A. At resonance $X_L=X_C=1/(\omega C)=1/(200\times2\times10^{-6})=2500\,\Omega$, so $V_L=IX_L=0.1\times2500=250$ V.

questions.q: A capacitor and an inductance coil are connected in separate AC circuits with a bulb glowing in both the circuits. The bulb glows more brightly when .....................
options: separation between the plates of the capacitor is increased.
a dielectric is introduced into the gap between the plates of the capacitor.
an iron rod is introduced into the inductance coil.
the number of turns in the inductance coil is increased.
questions.explanation: Introducing a dielectric increases the capacitor's capacitance, lowering $X_C=1/\omega C$ and increasing the current, so the bulb brightens; the other changes increase reactance and dim the bulb.

questions.q: An ideal choke draws a current of 8A when connected to an AC supply of 100 V, 50 Hz. A pure resistor draws a current of 10 A when connected to the same source. The ideal choke and the resistor are connected in series and then connected to the AC source of 150 V, 40 Hz. The current in the circuit becomes .....................
A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series with an a.c. source. If the potential drop across the capacitor is 5 V and that across resistor is 12 V, the applied voltage is
Ferromagnetic materials used in a transformer must have
options: high permeability and low hysterisis loss
high permeability and high hysterisis loss
low permeability and low hysterisis loss
low permeability and high hysterisis loss
questions.explanation: A transformer core needs high permeability (to concentrate flux efficiently) and low hysteresis loss (to minimise energy dissipated as heat per cycle).
